summary:
## Idea
Game.Core owns axial/cube coordinates, hex neighbours, ranges, rotations and coordinate conversions. Index the existing module instead of extracting a second implementation.

## Complexity
Basic coordinate arithmetic/distance is O(1); a radius-r range contains O(r²) cells, a ring O(r), and line drawing scales with endpoint distance. Search additionally depends on its visited budget.

## Use when
A .NET game already uses Game.Core Hex and needs its coordinate conventions.

## Avoid when
The supported JavaScript source view is required: the current profile explicitly excludes Hex.

## Pitfalls
Cube coordinates satisfy q+r+s=0; use tryCreateCube for validation. Float rounding is distinct from exact integer coordinates. ADR target grades do not override current DotNetOnly status.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Game.Core; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Game.Core.Hex.distance: Hex -> Hex -> int`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Game.Core
let destination = Hex.create 2 -1
let distance = Hex.distance Hex.origin destination
```

## Tests
HexTests is the cited existing property/case suite; compatibility-profile explicitly grades Hex DotNetOnly. No new Fable qualification is claimed.

## Bench
Owed: technique-specific timing baseline under https://github.com/FS-GG/FS.GG.Game/issues/804. No timing or cross-runtime performance claim is made here.

## References
Amit Patel, Hexagonal Grids, Red Blob Games (online reference, date not pinned): https://www.redblobgames.com/grids/hexagons/ . The cited Game.Core signature defines its own conversions and rounding; ADR0098 preserves Game.Core ownership.
